concepts.name: Retain
concepts.normative: Keep the selected existing surface and its supported semantics available while migration candidates are tested. Retention does not reapprove its implementation or expand its guarantees.
concepts.formal: retain(x) => remove(x)=false and supported_behavior(x) preserved within the selected profile
concepts.example: Preserve TDE obligation keys and BTE/SFOL entry points.
concepts.boundary: Local migration disposition, not a new canonical DomainSpec type

concepts.name: Adapt
concepts.normative: Introduce a separately testable successor boundary that preserves declared valid-input semantics and makes unsupported or invalid inputs explicit, without editing frozen sources.
concepts.plain: Repair the interface while preserving the meaning of valid inputs.
concepts.example: Add checked derivation that rejects parser violations instead of discarding them.
concepts.boundary: Diagnostics may improve only as explicitly declared; no implicit caller cutover

concepts.name: Retire
concepts.normative: Propose ending a precisely named compatibility surface only after its consumers, replacement coverage and rollback are demonstrated, followed by a separate explicit removal/cutover decision.
concepts.formal: retirement_eligible(x) => exact_consumers(x) and replacement_tested(x) and rollback_defined(x); eligible != authorized
concepts.plain: Remove nothing until replacement and recovery are proven and removal is authorized.
concepts.example: Replace obsolete changed-file selection only after all selected path cases pass.
concepts.boundary: Existing DROP exclusions remain exclusions; this pack grants no deletion

concepts.name: Compatibility envelope
concepts.normative: Name the exact input dialect, selected source bytes, existing profile and derivation identity, outputs, diagnostics and consumer for every comparison.
concepts.plain: State exactly which old behavior a successor must preserve.
concepts.example: Compare the sample aspect fixture against its existing legacy derivation; do not compare its count with a different machine profile.

concepts.name: Obligation correspondence
concepts.normative: Reuse the existing selected derivation and its obligation identities. A bridge preserves each obligation and reports unmapped or unsupported material explicitly; it does not reconstruct obligations through generated Markdown or infer parity from equal counts.
concepts.formal: mapped(O_source)=O_bridge with identities and semantic payloads preserved; unmapped != passed; different profiles require explicit correspondence
concepts.plain: Carry existing checks across without inventing or dropping checks.
concepts.example: Keep legacy SHA1 keys from source_anchor, rule_type and canonical_params; preserve the existing EVF S1 fixed obligation ID within that separate profile.
concepts.boundary: No hash algorithm replacement or new obligation denominator
